name: Riak KV
tagline: Erlang-based, Dynamo-style key-value store built to stay up through ugly failures.
description: Riak KV is a masterless, Dynamo-inspired key-value database written in Erlang: consistent hashing spreads data over a ring, sloppy quorums and hinted handoff keep writes flowing through node failures, and active anti-entropy repairs divergence in the background. Basho, its creator, collapsed in 2017; bet365 bought the IP and open-sourced the enterprise replication features, and development now continues as OpenRiak in conjunction with the Erlang Ecosystem Foundation, with 3.4.x releases in 2026. It is still a solid choice for high-availability blob and record storage where you can live with eventual consistency, but its ecosystem is small compared to Cassandra or DynamoDB.

pricing.notes: Free; commercial support available from independent consultancies.

scale.notes: Ring-based partitioning; multi-datacenter replication (formerly enterprise-only) is open source since 2.2.5/3.0.

strengths: Masterless ring keeps accepting writes during node and network failures
Active anti-entropy and read repair heal replicas automatically
Built-in CRDT data types (counters, sets, maps) for conflict-free merges
Erlang/OTP gives predictable behaviour under overload
weaknesses: Eventual consistency forces applications to handle siblings or use CRDTs
Small community and few client libraries are actively maintained
No rich query language; secondary indexes are basic
Basho-era documentation and tooling are dated
useCases: Highly available session and profile storage
Healthcare or betting systems needing extreme uptime
